HTTP API endpoint reference.
Check POST /v1/check Config GET /v1/config Container Details GET /v1/containers/details Containers GET /v1/containers Events GET /v1/events Health GET /v1/health History GET /v1/history Images GET /v1/images Metrics Prometheus metrics Status GET /v1/status Swagger UI OpenAPI / Swagger Update POST /v1/update

data.configuration#Configuration: Setting Flag Environment Variable Default Check API timeout --http-api-check-timeout WATCHTOWER_HTTP_API_CHECK_TIMEOUT 5m
data.container-name#Container Name:
The container parameter filters the check to only include specific containers by container name.
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer API_TOKEN" "localhost:8080/v1/check?container=nginx"
data.http-status-codes#HTTP Status Codes: Status Code Description 200 Check completed successfully 401 Invalid or missing authentication token 500 Internal server error during request processing
data.image-name#Image Name:
The image parameter filters the check to only include containers running specific image names.
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer API_TOKEN" "localhost:8080/v1/check?image=org/app:1.0" Replace API_TOKEN with your HTTP API token.
data.overview#Overview:
The v1/check endpoint enables checking monitored containers for available image updates.
Containers on the registry path are checked by querying the registry for the latest digest (HTTP HEAD with GET fallback). Containers associated for Git monitoring use the same watch split as scheduled updates. Watchtower reports whether the hosted Git ref is stale. It does not clone or build.
It does not download image layers and does not check against the configured image cooldown, as the cooldown functionality remains an apply-time gate for scheduled updates and /v1/update.
When no-pull is enabled globally or via the container label, a registry-path container is checked against the local image cache only. The registry is not contacted. A Git-watched container is not checked. The Git remote is not contacted, and the result is update_available: false.
Include check in http-api-endpoints to enable this endpoint.
data.response-format#Response Format:
The /v1/check endpoint returns a JSON array of container check results:
{ "containers": [ { "name": "nginx", "image": "nginx:latest", "image_id": "sha256:abc...", "digest": "sha256:old...", "update_available": true, "latest_image_id": "", "latest_digest": "sha256:new...", "update_source": "registry", "git_repo": "https://github.com/org/app.git", "git_ref": "main", "git_commit": "abc123def456", "changelog": "https://github.com/org/app/releases", "oci_source": "https://github.com/org/app", "current_image_version": "1.2.3", "current_revision": "1111111111", "timestamp": "2025-01-20T11:30:45Z" } ], "count": 1, "timestamp": "2025-01-20T11:30:45Z", "api_version": "v1" } name: Container name image: Current image reference with tag image_id: Current local image ID digest: Current local registry digest when known update_available: Whether a newer image is available latest_image_id: Local image ID of the newer image when known. It is empty for Git checks, which do not build or pull an image git_commit: Resolved Git commit for a Git-watched container when known latest_digest: Newest registry digest when known error: Per-container error message when the check failed update_source: registry or git (the staleness path; not OCI source) git_repo, git_ref, changelog: Resolved Git metadata when present oci_source, image_url, documentation: OCI image annotations when present current_image_version, current_revision: OCI version and revision of the running image when present No latest version here This endpoint never pulls an image, so latest_image_version and latest_revision are always empty. Use update_available and latest_digest to detect a pending update, and read the new version from a notification template after the update session runs. Containers associated for Git watching use the same watch split as scheduled updates. The check does not clone or build. See Git Monitoring. Git and OCI report fields are documented under notification templates.
data.sse-events#SSE Events:
When the /v1/events SSE endpoint is also enabled, execution of the v1/check endpoint broadcasts the following events:
scan_started: Broadcasted before the check begins scan_completed: Broadcasted after the check finishes successfully scan_failed: Broadcasted if the check encounters an error The scan_completed payload always reports updated: 0 because no updates are applied. The failed field counts containers whose per-container check returned an error.
data.timeout#Timeout:
The timeout parameter overrides the per-request timeout for this check. It accepts Go durations such as 30s, 2m, or 5m. The value is capped by the configured check API timeout (--http-api-check-timeout / WATCHTOWER_HTTP_API_CHECK_TIMEOUT, default 5m).
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer API_TOKEN" "localhost:8080/v1/check?timeout=2m"

data.http-status-codes#HTTP Status Codes: Status Code Description 200 Configuration retrieved successfully 401 Invalid or missing authentication token 500 Internal server error during request processing
data.overview#Overview:
The v1/config endpoint returns the active Watchtower configuration settings. Sensitive values (notification URLs, tokens) are redacted.
Include config in http-api-endpoints to enable this endpoint.
data.response-format#Response Format:
The /v1/config endpoint returns the current configuration:
{ "config": { "monitor_only": false, "cleanup": true, "no_pull": false, "no_restart": false, "rolling_restart": false, "include_stopped": false, "include_restarting": false, "lifecycle_hooks": false, "label_enable": false, "filter_desc": "", "scope": "", "git_enable": false }, "timestamp": "2025-01-20T11:30:45Z", "api_version": "v1" } Field Type Description monitor_only boolean Whether Watchtower is in monitor-only mode cleanup boolean Whether old images are removed after updating no_pull boolean Whether image pulling is disabled no_restart boolean Whether container restarting is disabled rolling_restart boolean Whether containers are restarted one at a time include_stopped boolean Whether stopped containers are included include_restarting boolean Whether restarting containers are included lifecycle_hooks boolean Whether lifecycle hooks are enabled label_enable boolean Whether label-based enabling is active filter_desc string Human-readable description of the applied filter scope string Monitoring scope git_enable boolean Process-wide Git watcher default Tokens, passwords, and SSH key paths are never included.

data.container-name#Container Name:
The name parameter filters results to a specific container by exact name.
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer API_TOKEN" "localhost:8080/v1/containers/details?name=nginx" Replace API_TOKEN with your HTTP API token.
data.http-status-codes#HTTP Status Codes: Status Code Description 200 Container details retrieved successfully 401 Invalid or missing authentication token 500 Internal server error during request processing
data.image-name#Image Name:
The image parameter filters results to containers running a specific image.
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer API_TOKEN" "localhost:8080/v1/containers/details?image=nginx:latest"
data.overview#Overview:
The /v1/containers/details endpoint returns detailed information about each watched container, including running state, image identity, and configuration flags.
Include containers in http-api-endpoints to enable this endpoint (container details are enabled alongside the containers list).
data.response-format#Response Format:
The /v1/containers/details endpoint returns a JSON array of container details:
{ "containers": [ { "name": "nginx", "image": "nginx:latest", "image_id": "sha256:1111...", "digest": "sha256:2222...", "running": true, "watchtower": false, "monitor_only": false, "no_pull": false, "enabled": true, "stale": false, "scope": "" } ], "count": 1, "timestamp": "2025-01-20T11:30:45Z", "api_version": "v1" } name: Container name image: Image reference with tag image_id: Local image config ID (sha256:…) digest: Registry manifest digest (sha256:…) for the repository in image, or the first digest when none matches it. Empty for locally-built images. running: Whether the container is currently running watchtower: Whether this is the Watchtower container itself monitor_only: Whether the container is in monitor-only mode no_pull: Whether image pulling is disabled for this container enabled: Whether the container is enabled for watching stale: Whether the container’s image is outdated scope: Monitoring scope of the container

data.container-name#Container Name:
The name parameter filters results to a specific container by exact name.
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer API_TOKEN" "localhost:8080/v1/containers?name=nginx" Replace API_TOKEN with your HTTP API token.
data.image-name#Image Name:
The image parameter filters results to containers running a specific image.
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer API_TOKEN" "localhost:8080/v1/containers?image=nginx:latest"
data.overview#Overview:
The /v1/containers endpoint lists monitored containers along with their current image ID.
Include containers in http-api-endpoints to enable this read-only endpoint.
data.response-format#Response Format:
The /v1/containers endpoint returns a JSON array of watched containers:
{ "containers": [ { "name": "nginx", "image": "nginx:latest", "image_id": "sha256:1111...", "digest": "sha256:2222..." } ], "count": 1, "timestamp": "2025-01-20T11:30:45Z", "api_version": "v1" } name: Container name image: Image reference with tag image_id: Local image config ID digest: Registry manifest digest the image was pulled from Taken from the image’s RepoDigests and comparable to a registry’s Docker-Content-Digest For an image with digests from several repositories, the one for the container’s image repository, or the first digest when none matches it Empty for locally built images with no registry reference Combine endpoints in one allowlist (for example containers,update,metrics) via http-api-endpoints.

data.authentication#Authentication:
The events endpoint requires authentication via the HTTP API Events Token configuration option.
This token can be provided in two formats:
Header-based auth — For programmatic clients using curl, fetch, etc.:
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer EVENTS_TOKEN" "http://localhost:8080/v1/events" Replace EVENTS_TOKEN with your events token.
Query-parameter auth — For browser EventSource API, which cannot send custom headers:
const eventSource = new EventSource('http://localhost:8080/v1/events?access_token=' + encodeURIComponent('EVENTS_TOKEN')); eventSource.addEventListener('scan_started', (e) => { console.log('Scan started:', JSON.parse(e.data)); }); eventSource.addEventListener('scan_completed', (e) => { console.log('Scan completed:', JSON.parse(e.data)); }); curl -N -G --data-urlencode "access_token=EVENTS_TOKEN" "http://localhost:8080/v1/events" The events endpoint uses a separate token from the main API token to limit blast radius, since query parameters may appear in access logs, browser history, and proxy logs.
data.event-format#Event Format:
Each event is a Server-Sent Event with an event type and JSON data payload:
event: scan_completed data: {"type":"scan_completed","timestamp":"2025-01-20T11:30:45Z","data":{"scanned":8,"updated":0,"failed":0,"skipped":0}}
data.http-status-codes#HTTP Status Codes: Status Code Description 200 Event stream established 401 Invalid or missing authentication token 403 Origin not allowed
data.overview#Overview:
The /v1/events endpoint streams Watchtower operational events via Server-Sent Events (SSE). Include events in http-api-endpoints to enable this endpoint.
Not usable via Swagger UI Try it out
Swagger UI will show a permanent Loading spinner on this endpoint even after successful authentication. The UI uses fetch and expects a finished response body; SSE is an open stream. Use curl -N or browser EventSource as shown below (see also Swagger UI).
data.supported-events#Supported Events:
Each event is sent under its type as the SSE event name:
Event Sent data fields scan_started Before an update session or a check begins The update policy as booleans: cleanup, no_restart, monitor_only, lifecycle_hooks, rolling_restart, label_precedence, no_pull, run_once, use_compose_depends_on, skip_self_update, ephemeral_self_update, revive_stopped scan_completed After an update session or a check ends without an error scanned, updated, failed, skipped scan_failed When an update session or a check ends with an error error image_cleanup After an update session removes old images images, each with image_id, image_name, container_id and container_name Update sessions are scheduled runs and /v1/update requests. Checks are /v1/check requests. A check updates nothing, so it never sends image_cleanup, and its scan_completed reports updated as 0.

data.endpoints#Endpoints: Name Method Endpoint Auth Description Liveness GET /livez No Returns 200 OK when the server is running Readiness GET /readyz No Returns 200 OK when Docker client is connected, 503 otherwise Startup GET /startupz No Returns 200 OK once the server has started
data.overview#Overview: Watchtower provides three health probe endpoints. Include health in http-api-endpoints to enable them.

data.combining-parameters#Combining Parameter:
Parameters can be combined to query a specific time range with a limit:
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer API_TOKEN" "localhost:8080/v1/history?since=2025-01-20T11:00:00Z&until=2025-01-20T12:00:00Z&limit=50"
data.http-status-codes#HTTP Status Codes: Status Code Description 200 History retrieved successfully 400 Invalid query parameter 401 Invalid or missing authentication token 500 Internal server error during request processing
data.limit#Limit:
The limit parameter restricts the maximum number of entries returned.
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer API_TOKEN" "localhost:8080/v1/history?limit=10"
data.overview#Overview: The /v1/history endpoint returns historical scan results from an in-memory ring buffer (up to 500 entries). Include history in http-api-endpoints to enable this read-only endpoint.
data.response-format#Response Format:
The /v1/history endpoint returns a JSON object with scan history entries:
{ "entries": [ { "timestamp": "2025-01-20T11:30:45Z", "scanned": 8, "updated": 0, "failed": 0, "restarted": 0, "skipped": 2 } ], "count": 1, "timestamp": "2025-01-20T11:35:00Z", "api_version": "v1" } An entry for a scan that ended in an error also has "scan_failed": true, and its counts are those the scan reached. The field is omitted for other scans.
data.since#Since:
The since parameter filters entries to those at or after the specified RFC3339 timestamp.
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer API_TOKEN" "localhost:8080/v1/history?since=2025-01-20T11:00:00Z" Replace API_TOKEN with your HTTP API token.
data.until#Until:
The until parameter filters entries to those at or before the specified RFC3339 timestamp.
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer API_TOKEN" "localhost:8080/v1/history?until=2025-01-20T12:00:00Z"

data.http-status-codes#HTTP Status Codes: Status Code Description 200 Images retrieved successfully 401 Invalid or missing authentication token 500 Internal server error during request processing
data.image-id#Image ID:
The id parameter filters results to a specific image by its image ID.
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer API_TOKEN" "localhost:8080/v1/images?id=IMAGE_ID" Replace IMAGE_ID with the image ID, such as the value of image_id in a response.
data.image-name#Image Name:
The name parameter filters results to a specific image by exact name.
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer API_TOKEN" "localhost:8080/v1/images?name=nginx:latest" Replace API_TOKEN with your HTTP API token.
data.overview#Overview: The /v1/images endpoint lists the images tracked by Watchtower along with their current digests and container counts. Include images in http-api-endpoints to enable this read-only endpoint.
data.response-format#Response Format:
The /v1/images endpoint returns a JSON object with image statuses, sorted by image name and then by image ID:
{ "images": [ { "name": "nginx:latest", "image_id": "sha256:1111...", "digest": "sha256:2222...", "containers": 3 } ], "count": 1, "timestamp": "2025-01-20T11:30:45Z", "api_version": "v1" } name: Image name with tag image_id: Local image config ID (sha256:…) digest: Registry manifest digest (sha256:…) for the repository in name, or the first digest when none matches it. Empty for locally-built images. containers: Number of watched containers using this image

data.available-metrics#Available Metrics:
Name Type Description watchtower_containers_scanned Gauge Number of containers scanned for changes during the last scan watchtower_containers_updated Gauge Number of containers updated during the last scan watchtower_containers_failed Gauge Number of containers where update failed during the last scan watchtower_containers_restarted_total Counter Number of containers restarted due to linked dependencies since watchtower started watchtower_containers_skipped Gauge Number of containers skipped during the last scan watchtower_scans_total Counter Number of scans since watchtower started watchtower_scans_skipped_total Counter Number of skipped scans since watchtower started watchtower_scans_failed_total Counter Number of scans that ended in an error since watchtower started watchtower_docker_images_bytes Gauge Docker image storage usage in bytes from the last disk-space check watchtower_docker_images_reclaimable_bytes Gauge Reclaimable Docker image storage in bytes from the last disk-space check watchtower_disk_space_max_bytes Gauge Configured Docker image-usage maximum in bytes (0 if unset) watchtower_disk_space_warn_bytes Gauge Configured Docker image-usage warning threshold in bytes (0 if unset) A scan is skipped when a scheduled run starts while the previous one is still running, or when the update at startup finds another update already running. A skipped scan does not change the scan total or the last-scan gauges.
The four image-usage gauges are updated when disk-space-max or disk-space-warn are set. See Disk Usage Monitor.
data.demo#Demo: The repository contains an example deployment with Prometheus and Grafana, available through /examples/metrics/docker-compose.yml. This demo is preconfigured with a dashboard, which will look something like this:
data.example-prometheus-scrape_config#Example: scrape_configs: - job_name: watchtower scrape_interval: 15s metrics_path: /v1/metrics bearer_token: API_TOKEN static_configs: - targets: - 'watchtower:8080' Replace API_TOKEN with your HTTP API token.
data.overview#Overview:
The /v1/metrics endpoint provides Prometheus-compatible metrics.
To use this feature, set an API token, include metrics in http-api-endpoints, and map container port 8080.
Enable multiple endpoints in one allowlist (for example metrics,update) via http-api-endpoints. Enabling the metrics API with port mappings will automatically disable Watchtower’s self-update functionality to prevent port conflicts during container recreation. See Updating Watchtower for more details. The /v1/metrics endpoint only accepts GET requests. Requests with other HTTP methods will receive a 405 Method Not Allowed response.

data.http-status-codes#HTTP Status Codes: Status Code Description 200 Status retrieved successfully 204 No scan has been performed yet 401 Invalid or missing authentication token 500 Internal server error during request processing
data.overview#Overview: The /v1/status endpoint returns a summary of the most recent Watchtower scan, including counts of scanned, updated, failed, restarted, and skipped containers. Include metrics in http-api-endpoints to enable it (the status endpoint is enabled alongside metrics).
data.response-format#Response Format:
The /v1/status endpoint returns a JSON scan summary:
{ "summary": { "scanned": 8, "updated": 0, "failed": 0, "restarted": 0, "skipped": 2 }, "timestamp": "2025-01-20T11:30:45Z", "api_version": "v1" } scanned: Number of containers scanned updated: Number of containers successfully updated failed: Number of containers where the update failed restarted: Number of containers restarted skipped: Number of containers skipped scan_failed: true when the scan ended in an error. The counts are then those the scan reached. Omitted for other scans timestamp: UTC timestamp of the last scan (RFC3339 format) If no scan has been performed yet, the endpoint returns HTTP 204 (No Content).

data.endpoint#Endpoint: Name Method Endpoint Auth Description Swagger GET /swagger/* No Interactive API documentation rendered via Swagger UI The endpoint is mounted as a wildcard route (/swagger/) so that all Swagger UI assets are served under this prefix. Accessing /swagger/index.html returns the main documentation page and sub-paths serve the static assets the UI needs.
data.openapi-specification#OpenAPI Specificat:
The UI is powered by a machine-readable OpenAPI Specification (OAS) document that describes every enabled Watchtower endpoint. This project uses the Swagger 2.0 format (OAS 2.0), rendered as swagger.json and swagger.yaml.
Swagger UI renders the spec as CommonMark in most tooltip and description fields, per the OAS rich text requirements .
data.overview#Overview:
The /swagger/ endpoint serves an interactive, browser-based Swagger UI that renders the Watchtower HTTP API specification.
To enable the Swagger UI, include swagger in http-api-endpoints (for example WATCHTOWER_HTTP_API_ENDPOINTS=swagger or all).
data.query-parameters#Query parameters:
Swagger UI exposes any @Param query parameters documented in the spec.
For example, the /v1/update endpoint accepts the following documented query parameters:
Parameter Type Required Description image string No Comma-separated image names or Go regex patterns to filter. container string No Comma-separated container name patterns to filter. async boolean No Run the update asynchronously; returns 202 Accepted when true.
data.references#References: OpenAPI Specification 3.1.1 — the normative specification that defines the structure OAS documents (Swagger 2.0 is a prior version of the same standard; see OAS Learn ) Swagger UI — official tooling — the open-source UI that renders the interactive documentation gofiber/contrib/v3/swaggo — Fiber v3 integration middleware that serves the UI and spec swaggo/swag — the Go annotation parser and code generator that produces the OpenAPI 2.0 spec from handler comments
data.reverse-proxy-and-tls-termination#Revers:
When Watchtower runs behind a TLS-terminating reverse proxy (Traefik, Caddy, Nginx, etc.), Swagger UI’s Try it out generates request URLs from the OpenAPI spec schemes field.
The spec schemes value is derived from c.Protocol(). Fiber v3 only trusts X-Forwarded-Proto from a client when that client IP is listed in http-api-trusted-proxies. If the proxy IP is not trusted, c.Protocol() reports http even though the external connection uses HTTPS, and Swagger UI will generate http:// URLs.
To ensure correct scheme detection:
Set http-api-trusted-proxies to include the proxy IP or CIDR range. Ensure http-api-proxy-header matches the header your proxy uses (default: X-Forwarded-For). This is the same trusted-proxies configuration used for client IP detection and rate limiting, so it is not specific to Swagger.
data.security#Security:
The Swagger UI page does not require authentication to access.
Calling protected APIs via Try it out still requires the http-api-token (or events token for /v1/events) through Swagger UI’s Authorize control. That is the same protection as any other client.
The same guidance that applies to the rest of the HTTP API applies here as well:
Never expose the HTTP API (including the Swagger UI) directly to the Internet — the UI documents every route surface. Always use TLS. Only enable the endpoints you actually need. If you place the API behind a reverse proxy (Traefik, Caddy, Nginx, etc.), configure trusted proxies and CORS origins accordingly.
data.starting-the-server#Starting the Server:
Enable the endpoint and start Watchtower:
Without TLSWith TLS Docker ComposeDocker CLI services: watchtower: image: nickfedor/watchtower:latest volumes: - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock environment: - WATCHTOWER_HTTP_API_ENDPOINTS=swagger - WATCHTOWER_HTTP_API_TOKEN=API_TOKEN ports: - "8080:8080" restart: unless-stopped docker run -d \ --name watchtower \ -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \ -e WATCHTOWER_HTTP_API_ENDPOINTS=swagger \ -e WATCHTOWER_HTTP_API_TOKEN=API_TOKEN \ -p 8080:8080 \ --restart unless-stopped \ nickfedor/watchtower Then open the Swagger UI in a web browser:
http://HOST:8080/swagger/index.html Replace the following:
API_TOKEN: the token that clients must send to the HTTP API HOST: the host name or IP address of the Docker host Docker ComposeDocker CLI services: watchtower: image: nickfedor/watchtower:latest volumes: - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock - /opt/watchtower/certs:/certs:ro environment: - WATCHTOWER_HTTP_API_ENDPOINTS=swagger - WATCHTOWER_HTTP_API_TOKEN=API_TOKEN - WATCHTOWER_HTTP_API_TLS_CERT=/certs/watchtower.crt - WATCHTOWER_HTTP_API_TLS_KEY=/certs/watchtower.key ports: - "8080:8080" restart: unless-stopped docker run -d \ --name watchtower \ -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \ -v /opt/watchtower/certs:/certs:ro \ -e WATCHTOWER_HTTP_API_ENDPOINTS=swagger \ -e WATCHTOWER_HTTP_API_TOKEN=API_TOKEN \ -e WATCHTOWER_HTTP_API_TLS_CERT=/certs/watchtower.crt \ -e WATCHTOWER_HTTP_API_TLS_KEY=/certs/watchtower.key \ -p 8080:8080 \ --restart unless-stopped \ nickfedor/watchtower Then open the Swagger UI in a web browser:
https://HOST:8080/swagger/index.html Replace the following:
API_TOKEN: the token that clients must send to the HTTP API HOST: the host name of the Docker host, as named in the certificate
data.troubleshooting#Troubleshooting:
The /swagger/* endpoint and Swagger UI return standard HTTP status codes.
Common issues and their resolutions:
HTTP Status Cause Resolution 404 The endpoint may not be enabled Include swagger in http-api-endpoints. 404 Requested a path outside /swagger/*, e.g. /swagger (no wildcard). Navigate to /swagger/index.html. 405 HTTP method other than GET used against /swagger/*. Use GET only. POST, PUT, and DELETE are not supported on this path. The server startup log confirms successful registration:
2026/07/06 20:00:00 [INFO] HTTP API listening on :8080
data.try-it-out#Try it out:
Swagger UI’s Try it out button issues a real HTTP request from your browser directly to the Watchtower server. Because Swagger UI is served from the same origin, no CORS preflight is required when both are accessed from the same host and port (the default setup). When the UI is served from a different origin, ensure the http-api-cors-origins configuration option allows the browser origin.
JSON endpoints (/v1/config, /v1/containers, /v1/check, etc.) work well with Try it out. The events SSE stream does not (see the warning above).
data.try-it-out-call-protected-apis-from-the-:
Open http://HOST:PORT/swagger/index.html (or https:// when TLS is enabled), where HOST and PORT are the address and port of the HTTP API. Click Authorize at the top-right of Swagger UI. Under BearerAuth, paste the HTTP API token only (do not type the word Bearer. Swagger UI places the value in the Authorization header). For /v1/events, under EventsToken, paste the events token only (auth works in Try it out, but the stream itself will not — see below). Click Authorize, then Close. Use Try it out on an operation (except the events stream). Authorization for Try it out is persisted across page reloads when using Swagger UI’s persist-authorization setting.
Programmatic clients should still use Authorization: Bearer API_TOKEN (or the events token header/query form); see Authentication.
Events SSE is not supported in Swagger UI
Try it out on /v1/events will authenticate, then hang on a permanent Loading spinner. That is a Swagger UI limitation, not a Watchtower bug.
Swagger UI uses the browser fetch API and waits for a finished HTTP body. An SSE response is an open stream of text/event-stream events with no single “complete” body, so the UI never finishes rendering.
Use one of these instead:
# curl (keep the connection open with -N) curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $WATCHTOWER_HTTP_API_EVENTS_TOKEN" \ "http://localhost:8080/v1/events" // Browser EventSource (query token; EventSource cannot set Authorization headers) const es = new EventSource( "http://localhost:8080/v1/events?access_token=" + encodeURIComponent(eventsToken) ); es.onmessage = (e) => console.log(e.data); Full details: Events.
data.under-the-hood#Under the Hood:
The Swagger 2.0 specification is generated from annotions in the codebase using swaggo/swag .
Then, Fiber v3’s gofiber/contrib/v3/swaggo middleware package is used to serve the bundled Swagger UI assets and generated specification.
The generated files (docs.go, swagger.json, swagger.yaml) can be found in the repository at https://github.com/nicholas-fedor/watchtower/tree/main/internal/api/swagger .

data.asynchronous-update-trigger#Asynchronous:
Adding the ?async=true parameter to a POST request causes the handler to spawn the update in a background goroutine and return immediately with HTTP 202 Accepted.
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer API_TOKEN" "localhost:8080/v1/update?async=true" Response:
HTTP/1.1 202 Accepted Content-Type: application/json Equivalent example for a targeted async update:
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer API_TOKEN" "localhost:8080/v1/update?image=org/app:latest&async=true" The same concurrency behavior applies to async requests: full updates return 429 if another update is already in progress, while targeted updates block until the lock is available before spawning the async goroutine.
data.asynchronous-updates#Asynchronous Update: The /v1/update endpoint supports an async query parameter to trigger updates without waiting for completion. This is useful for CI environments or automation that needs to fire-and-forget without maintaining a long-lived connection.
data.concurrency-behavior#Concurrency Behavio:
The /v1/update endpoint handles concurrent requests differently based on whether targeted or full updates are being performed:
Full Updates (no ?image= or ?container= parameter):
Returns HTTP 429 immediately if another update is already in progress Includes a Retry-After: 30 header suggesting when to retry the request Does not block or wait for the existing update to complete Targeted Updates (with ?image= or ?container= parameter):
Blocks until the update lock is available Waits for any in-progress update to complete before proceeding Does not return HTTP 429 This behavior ensures that full updates (which may be resource-intensive) are not queued up, while targeted updates (which are typically faster) can wait for their turn.
data.configuration#Configuration: Setting Flag Environment Variable Default Update API timeout --http-api-update-timeout WATCHTOWER_HTTP_API_UPDATE_TIMEOUT 10m
data.container-name#Container Name: Watchtower supports using the container URL query parameter to filter updates for only certain containers by name.
data.container-name-patterns#Container Name P:
You can specify exact container names or Go regex patterns to match containers.
For example, to update only containers with names starting with web-:
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer API_TOKEN" "localhost:8080/v1/update?container=^web-.*"
data.error-response-format#Error Response For:
When an error occurs, the API returns a JSON response with the following structure:
{ "error": "another update is already running", "api_version": "v1", "timestamp": "2025-01-20T11:30:45Z" } error: A human-readable error message describing what went wrong api_version: API version identifier timestamp: UTC timestamp when the error response was generated (RFC3339 format)
data.example#Example: services: app-monitored-by-watchtower: image: myapps/monitored-by-watchtower labels: - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true" watchtower: image: nickfedor/watchtower volumes: - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock environment: - WATCHTOWER_HTTP_API_TOKEN=API_TOKEN - WATCHTOWER_HTTP_API_ENDPOINTS=update,metrics labels: - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=false" ports: - 8080:8080 restart: unless-stopped Enable multiple endpoints in one allowlist (for example update,metrics) via http-api-endpoints. Enabling the HTTP API with port mappings will automatically disable Watchtower’s self-update functionality to prevent port conflicts during container recreation. See Updating Watchtower for more details.
data.http-status-codes#HTTP Status Codes:
The /v1/update endpoint returns the following HTTP status codes:
Status Code Description 200 Update completed successfully 202 Update triggered successfully and running asynchronously (with ?async=true) 401 Invalid or missing authentication token 429 Another update is already in progress (full updates only) or the request was rate limited 500 Internal server error during request processing 503 Update handler timed out (exceeded configured limit, default 10m), or client cancelled while waiting on update lock (targeted updates only)
data.image-filtering-with-tags#Image Filterin:
You can specify image tags to target containers running a specific version (e.g., org/app:1.0).
For example, to update only containers using org/app:1.0 and org/worker:latest:
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer API_TOKEN" "localhost:8080/v1/update?image=org/app:1.0,org/worker:latest"
data.image-filtering-without-tags#Image Filte:
If no tag is provided, Watchtower matches containers regardless of their tag.
The following curl command would trigger an update for the images org/app and org/worker:
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer API_TOKEN" "localhost:8080/v1/update?image=org/app,org/worker"
data.image-name#Image Name: Watchtower supports using the image URL query parameter to filter updates for only certain images.
data.metadata#Metadata: timestamp: UTC timestamp when the response was generated (RFC3339 format) api_version: API version identifier
data.multiple-container-patterns#Multiple Con:
Use commas to specify multiple patterns:
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer API_TOKEN" "localhost:8080/v1/update?container=^web-.*,^api-.*"
data.no-image-filtering#No Image Filtering:
The following curl command would trigger an update of all container images monitored by Watchtower:
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer API_TOKEN" "localhost:8080/v1/update" Replace API_TOKEN with your HTTP API token.
data.overview#Overview: Include update in http-api-endpoints to enable this mode.
data.rate-limiting#Rate Limiting:
Watchtower enforces two independent mechanisms that can each return HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests):
Per-IP request-rate limiting (applies globally to all HTTP API endpoints):
Every incoming request is checked against a per-IP rate limiter using a sliding window algorithm before authentication is evaluated. Default limit: 60 requests per minute. Configurable via the HTTP API Rate Limit configuration option. Rate-limited requests receive HTTP 429 with no body. Rate limit state is tracked per client IP address. Concurrency-based update limiting (applies only to /v1/update):
The /v1/update handler uses an internal lock to ensure only one update runs at a time. If a full update (no image or container query parameter) is requested while another update is already in progress, the handler immediately returns HTTP 429 with a JSON error body and a Retry-After: 30 header. Targeted updates (with image or container query parameter) block until the lock is available rather than returning 429. Precedence: Per-IP rate limiting is evaluated first. If a request passes the rate limit, it proceeds to the endpoint handler where concurrency limiting may apply for /v1/update.
data.regex-pattern-matching#Regex Pattern Mat:
Container patterns support Go regex syntax. Invalid regex patterns are treated as literal strings for exact matching.
Pattern Matches mycontainer Exact match for mycontainer ^web-.* Any name starting with web- .*-prod$ Any name ending with -prod
data.request-body-protection#Request Body Pro: Request bodies are capped at 1 MiB to prevent resource exhaustion from large uploads Requests exceeding this limit will be rejected with HTTP 413 (Payload Too Large)
data.response-format#Response Format:
The /v1/update endpoint returns a JSON response containing the results of the update operation:
{ "summary": { "scanned": 8, "updated": 0, "failed": 0, "restarted": 0, "skipped": 2 }, "timing": { "duration_ms": 1250, "duration": "1.25s" }, "timestamp": "2025-01-20T11:30:45Z", "api_version": "v1" }
data.sse-events#SSE Events:
When the /v1/events SSE endpoint is also enabled, the update process broadcasts the following events:
scan_started: Broadcasted before the update scan begins scan_completed: Broadcasted after the update scan finishes scan_failed: Broadcasted if the update scan encounters an error image_cleanup: Broadcasted after image cleanup if enabled and images were removed
data.status-codes-for-async-requests#Status C:
Status Code Description 202 Update triggered successfully and running asynchronously 401 Invalid or missing authentication token 429 Another update is already in progress (full updates only) or the request was rate limited 500 Internal server error during request processing 503 Update handler timed out (exceeded configured limit, default 10m), or client cancelled while waiting on update lock (targeted updates only) The following example shows what happens when a full update is requested while another update is already running:
curl -i -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer API_TOKEN" "localhost:8080/v1/update" Response:
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests Content-Type: application/json Retry-After: 30 { "error": "another update is already running", "api_version": "v1", "timestamp": "2025-01-20T11:30:45Z" } The client should wait at least 30 seconds (as indicated by the Retry-After header) before attempting another request.
data.summary-section#Summary Section: scanned: Number of containers that were scanned for updates updated: Number of containers that were successfully updated failed: Number of containers where the update failed restarted: Number of containers that were restarted due to linked dependencies skipped: Number of containers that were skipped during the update scan_failed: true when the update ended in an error. The counts are then those the update reached. Omitted otherwise
data.timeout#Timeout:
The timeout parameter overrides the per-request timeout for this update. It accepts Go durations such as 30s, 2m, or 10m. The value is capped by the configured update API timeout (--http-api-update-timeout / WATCHTOWER_HTTP_API_UPDATE_TIMEOUT, default 10m).
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer API_TOKEN" "localhost:8080/v1/update?timeout=15m" For synchronous updates, this bounds the time the HTTP response is held. For asynchronous updates (?async=true), this bounds how long the background update runs before being cancelled.
data.timing-section#Timing Section: duration_ms: Execution time in milliseconds duration: Human-readable execution time
data.update-handler-timeout#Update Handler Ti: The /v1/update handler has a timeout enforced by Fiber’s timeout middleware. The default is 10 minutes. The timeout covers the full lifecycle: waiting for the concurrency lock, performing the container update scan, and returning results. When the timeout is exceeded, the handler returns HTTP 503 (Service Unavailable) and the handler goroutine is abandoned. The handler listens on c.Context().Done() for cooperative cancellation — targeted updates waiting for the lock will return HTTP 503 when the request context is cancelled. You can override the timeout per request with the ?timeout= query parameter, up to the configured maximum.
data.using-the-http-api-and-periodic-updates#:
By default, enabling the HTTP API prevents periodic updates (i.e. scheduled or interval polling).
Use the HTTP API Periodic Polls configuration option to enable periodic updates while using the HTTP API.

data:
Watchtower has an optional HTTP API server that is enabled by configuring the http-api-endpoints and http-api-token configuration options and publishing the HTTP API port (default: 8080).
This HTTP API server extends Watchtower’s functionality by providing HTTP endpoints that allows for programmatic access to functionality, such as checking the current status of monitored containers and requesting Watchtower to perform container updates. Parameters, such as container and image name filters, can be used to further fine-tune HTTP requests.
Deprecation of HTTP API Endpoint Configuration Options
The following options have been deprecated in favor of the unified http-api-endpoints configuration option and will be removed with the v2.x.x release of Watchtower:
http-api-update http-api-containers http-api-metrics
data.endpoints#Endpoints:
The following endpoints can be enabled by using thehttp-api-endpoints configuration option and the respective configuration value.
Name Configuration Value Method Endpoint Auth Parameters Description Update update POST /v1/update API token image, container, async Triggers container updates and returns JSON results of the operation Check check POST /v1/check API token image, container Checks containers for available updates (registry digest or Git ref) Containers containers GET /v1/containers API token name, image Lists watched containers and their current running image digests Container Details containers GET /v1/containers/details API token name, image Returns detailed information about each watched container including running state and configuration flags History history GET /v1/history API token since, until, limit Returns historical scan results from the in-memory ring buffer (up to 500 entries) Images images GET /v1/images API token name, id Lists tracked images with their current digests and container counts Config config GET /v1/config API token Returns the active Watchtower configuration settings Events events GET /v1/events Events token Streams real-time operational events via Server-Sent Events Status metrics GET /v1/status API token Returns the summary of the most recent scan Metrics metrics GET /v1/metrics API token Exposes Prometheus-compatible metrics for monitoring and alerting Swagger swagger GET /swagger/* None Interactive API documentation via Swagger UI Liveness health GET /livez None Returns 200 OK when the server is running Readiness health GET /readyz None Returns 200 OK when Docker client is connected, 503 otherwise Startup health GET /startupz None Returns 200 OK once the server has started Endpoints enforce HTTP method restrictions using method-based routing. Requests with unsupported methods will receive a 405 Method Not Allowed response. Watchtower will not start if http-api-endpoints has incorrect values or is combined with all (which enables all endpoints).

data.security-considerations#Security conside:
Watchtower was originally designed to be a stateless application with direct access to the Docker socket. By having direct access to the Docker socket, the application effectively runs with root-level privileges. It is worth taking a moment to review and familiarize yourself with the Docker Engine security documentation and explore other security tools such as Docker socket proxies.
!!! Warning “The HTTP API should never be directly exposed to the Internet!” !!! Warning “Using the HTTP API without TLS encryption is insecure and not recommended!” !!! Warning “Only enable the endpoints that you need!” Authentication, TLS, trusted proxies, CORS, and rate limiting are covered under Authentication, TLS, and the HTTP API configuration reference.

data.overview#Overview:
Watchtower has a number of legacy notification configuration options that will be removed with the release of Watchtower v2.
This deprecation and eventual removal of legacy notification configuration options is a long-term migration that started with the refactoring of Shoutrrr into a separate notification library. The removal of the legacy notification configuration options is simply a removal of an unnecessary abstraction layer in favor of using Shoutrrr URL’s directly.
In order to continue receiving notifications, users will need to add Shoutrrr URL’s directly using the NOTIFICATION URL configuration option.
Watchtower users do not need to install any new software to implement Shoutrrr URL’s.
Use Watchtower’s CLI migration tool to help convert legacy email configurations to Shoutrrr URLs or use the Shoutrrr Playground to help convert configurations for other services to Shoutrrr URLs.

data.notes#Notes:
Timeout:
The default SMTP timeout is 10 seconds. If you experience timeouts (e.g., failed to send: timed out: using smtp), add &timeout=30s to the URL to allow more time for server responses, especially with proxies or slow networks. Authentication:
Use &auth=Plain for username and password authentication, including Gmail App Passwords . This is the default when credentials are provided. Set clientid, clientsecret, scopes and tokenurl to have Shoutrrr get OAuth2 access tokens with the client credentials grant , as the Microsoft 365 example does. Shoutrrr then uses OAuth2 without &auth=OAuth2. Use &auth=OAuth2 only for SASL XOAUTH2 with a static access token in the password field. App Passwords are not OAuth2. Testing:
Install Shoutrrr using one of the various installation methods .
Test your URL with the Shoutrrr CLI:
shoutrrr send -u "NOTIFICATION_URL" -m "Test message" Replace NOTIFICATION_URL with the smtp:// URL to test.
Proxy Issues:
If using a Docker proxy (e.g., tcp://dockerproxy:2375), ensure it allows outbound connections to your SMTP server’s host and port. Test connectivity with telnet SMTP_HOST SMTP_PORT inside the container. Replace SMTP_HOST with your SMTP server’s host name and SMTP_PORT with its port.

data.automated-migration-script#Automated Mig:
If you have a docker-compose.yaml with a watchtower service configured for legacy notifications, you can use the script below to run the entire migration process end-to-end. It starts the container, executes notify-upgrade, extracts the generated file, prints its contents, and cleans up.
#!/usr/bin/env bash set -euo pipefail SERVICE="${1:-watchtower}" OUTPUT="${2:-./watchtower-notifications.env}" CONTAINER=$(docker compose run -d "${SERVICE}" notify-upgrade) trap 'docker rm -f "${CONTAINER}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true' EXIT if ! docker ps -q --filter "id=${CONTAINER}" | grep -q .; then echo "notify-upgrade container exited before producing output. Logs:" >&2 docker logs "${CONTAINER}" >&2 || true exit 1 fi FILE="" TIMEOUT=300 INTERVAL=2 ELAPSED=0 while [[ ${ELAPSED} -lt ${TIMEOUT} ]]; do FILE=$(docker logs "${CONTAINER}" 2>&1 | grep -oE 'watchtower-notif-urls-[^ ]+' | tail -1 || true) if [[ -n "${FILE}" ]]; then break fi sleep "${INTERVAL}" ELAPSED=$((ELAPSED + INTERVAL)) done if [[ -z "${FILE}" ]]; then echo "Timed out waiting for notify-upgrade output. Logs:" >&2 docker logs "${CONTAINER}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true exit 1 fi docker cp "${CONTAINER}:${FILE}" "${OUTPUT}" echo "=== Generated Shoutrrr URL ===" cat "${OUTPUT}" The service must already be defined in docker-compose.yaml with your legacy notification environment variables. The script assumes the service name defaults to watchtower. The command will self-cleanup after 5 minutes or when the script exits. notify-upgrade keeps a Slack channel only when it is a Slack channel ID, such as C0123456789. A channel name such as #ops or a user such as @dana cannot be carried into the Shoutrrr URL, so the generated URL uses the webhook’s own channel and notify-upgrade logs a warning. Webhooks created by a Slack app always post to their own channel.
data.existing-deployment#Existing Deployment:
If Watchtower is already deployed and running with your legacy notification configuration, you can execute notify-upgrade directly inside the container:
docker exec watchtower /watchtower notify-upgrade This works because the Watchtower binary is installed at /watchtower and notify-upgrade is a built-in subcommand. The common mistake is running docker exec watchtower notify-upgrade, which fails because notify-upgrade is not a standalone executable in $PATH.
Running notify-upgrade inside an existing container does not stop or restart the main Watchtower process. docker exec runs a separate, short-lived process. The only side effect is that the notify-upgrade process will stay alive for up to 5 minutes while waiting for you to retrieve the temporary file, after which it cleans up and exits.
data.migration-walkthrough#Migration Walkthro:
Select the tab that matches your legacy notification service.
Email (SMTP)GotifySlackMicrosoft Teams 1. Run the following Docker Compose configuration / Docker CLI command:
Docker ComposeDocker CLI (Env Vars)Docker CLI (Flags) services: watchtower: image: nickfedor/watchtower:latest environment: WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATIONS: email WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER: smtp.example.com WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER_PORT: 587 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER_USER: USERNAME WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER_PASSWORD: 'PASSWORD' WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_FROM: sender@example.com WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_TO: recipient@example.com WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_DELAY: 10 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SUBJECTTAG: Watchtower volumes: - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock docker run -d \ --name watchtower \ -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \ -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATIONS=email \ -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER=smtp.example.com \ -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER_PORT=587 \ -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER_USER=USERNAME \ -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER_PASSWORD='PASSWORD' \ -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_FROM=sender@example.com \ -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_TO=recipient@example.com \ -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_DELAY=10 \ -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SUBJECTTAG=Watchtower \ nickfedor/watchtower docker run -d \ --name watchtower \ -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \ nickfedor/watchtower \ --notifications email \ --notification-email-server smtp.example.com \ --notification-email-server-port 587 \ --notification-email-server-user USERNAME \ --notification-email-server-password 'PASSWORD' \ --notification-email-from sender@example.com \ --notification-email-to recipient@example.com \ --notification-email-delay 10 \ --notification-email-subjecttag Watchtower Replace the following:
USERNAME: the user name for your SMTP server. notify-upgrade writes an @ in it as %40. PASSWORD: the password for your SMTP server, inside the single quotes. In a Compose file, write each ' in it as '' and each $ as $$. In a shell command, write each ' as '\''. Use your SMTP server’s host name in place of smtp.example.com and your own addresses in place of sender@example.com and recipient@example.com.
2. With the container running, execute the notify-upgrade command:
docker exec watchtower /watchtower notify-upgrade Then copy the resulting file out of the container with the command that notify-upgrade logs:
docker cp CONTAINER_ID:FILE_NAME ./watchtower-notifications.env 3. The following converted Shoutrrr URL should be produced:
smtp://USERNAME:PASSWORD@smtp.example.com:587/?auth=Plain&clienthost=localhost&encryption=Auto&fromaddress=sender%40example.com&fromname=Watchtower&subject=&toaddresses=recipient%40example.com&usehtml=No&usestarttls=Yes&timeout=10s 4. Replace the deprecated configuration with the converted Shoutrrr URL. The URL does not carry the email delay or the subject tag. Set the notifications delay and the title tag in their place:
Docker ComposeDocker CLI (Env Vars)Docker CLI (Flags) services: watchtower: image: nickfedor/watchtower:latest environment: WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_URL: 'smtp://USERNAME:PASSWORD@smtp.example.com:587/?auth=Plain&clienthost=localhost&encryption=Auto&fromaddress=sender%40example.com&fromname=Watchtower&subject=&toaddresses=recipient%40example.com&usehtml=No&usestarttls=Yes&timeout=10s' WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATIONS_DELAY: "10" WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_TITLE_TAG: Watchtower volumes: - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock docker run -d \ --name watchtower \ -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \ -e 'WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_URL=smtp://USERNAME:PASSWORD@smtp.example.com:587/?auth=Plain&clienthost=localhost&encryption=Auto&fromaddress=sender%40example.com&fromname=Watchtower&subject=&toaddresses=recipient%40example.com&usehtml=No&usestarttls=Yes&timeout=10s' \ -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATIONS_DELAY=10 \ -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_TITLE_TAG=Watchtower \ nickfedor/watchtower docker run -d \ --name watchtower \ -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \ nickfedor/watchtower \ --notification-url 'smtp://USERNAME:PASSWORD@smtp.example.com:587/?auth=Plain&clienthost=localhost&encryption=Auto&fromaddress=sender%40example.com&fromname=Watchtower&subject=&toaddresses=recipient%40example.com&usehtml=No&usestarttls=Yes&timeout=10s' \ --notifications-delay 10 \ --notification-title-tag Watchtower The single quotes keep YAML and the shell from changing the URL. `notify-upgrade` writes a `'` in the password as `%27` but leaves a `$` as it is. In a Compose file, write each `$` in the URL as `$$`. Avoid using unrecognized flags like WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER_SSL, as they are ignored and may cause confusion. Use the encryption and usestarttls URL parameters in the smtp:// URL to control TLS behavior rather than deprecated flags. 1. Run the following Docker Compose configuration / Docker CLI command:
Docker ComposeDocker CLI (Env Vars)Docker CLI (Flags) services: watchtower: image: nickfedor/watchtower:latest environment: WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATIONS: gotify WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_GOTIFY_URL: "https://gotify.example.com/" WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_GOTIFY_TOKEN: "TOKEN" WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_GOTIFY_TLS_SKIP_VERIFY: true volumes: - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock docker run -d \ --name watchtower \ -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \ -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATIONS=gotify \ -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_GOTIFY_URL="https://gotify.example.com/" \ -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_GOTIFY_TOKEN="TOKEN" \ -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_GOTIFY_TLS_SKIP_VERIFY=true \ nickfedor/watchtower docker run -d \ --name watchtower \ -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \ nickfedor/watchtower \ --notifications gotify \ --notification-gotify-url "https://gotify.example.com/" \ --notification-gotify-token "TOKEN" \ --notification-gotify-tls-skip-verify Replace TOKEN with the application token from your Gotify server and gotify.example.com with your server’s host name.
2. With the container running, execute the notify-upgrade command:
docker exec watchtower /watchtower notify-upgrade Then copy the resulting file out of the container with the command that notify-upgrade logs:
docker cp CONTAINER_ID:FILE_NAME ./watchtower-notifications.env 3. The following converted Shoutrrr URL should be produced:
gotify://gotify.example.com/TOKEN?skiptlsverify=Yes&title= 4. Replace the deprecated configuration with the converted Shoutrrr URL:
Docker ComposeDocker CLI (Env Vars)Docker CLI (Flags) services: watchtower: image: nickfedor/watchtower:latest environment: WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_URL: "gotify://gotify.example.com/TOKEN?skiptlsverify=Yes&title=" volumes: - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock docker run -d \ --name watchtower \ -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \ -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_URL="gotify://gotify.example.com/TOKEN?skiptlsverify=Yes&title=" \ nickfedor/watchtower docker run -d \ --name watchtower \ -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \ nickfedor/watchtower \ --notification-url "gotify://gotify.example.com/TOKEN?skiptlsverify=Yes&title=" 1. data.overview#Overview:
Watchtower includes a notify-upgrade command to help convert legacy notification configurations to Shoutrrr URLs for use with the NOTIFICATION URL.
It parses legacy Watchtower notification configurations and outputs Shoutrrr URLs to a temporary file inside the Watchtower container.
Settings the file leaves out The file holds only the notification URL. It leaves out two legacy email settings, which are not part of a Shoutrrr URL. Watchtower applies both while your legacy settings are in place. When you switch to the generated URL, set their replacements yourself:
notification-email-delay is replaced by notifications-delay. notification-email-subjecttag is replaced by notification-title-tag.
data.retrieving-the-generated-file#Retrieving:
After running notify-upgrade, the converted Shoutrrr URL is written to a temporary file in the container’s working directory. Its name starts with watchtower-notif-urls- and ends in a random number.
The command logs a copy command with the container and the file name:
INFO To get the environment file, use: docker cp CONTAINER_ID:FILE_NAME ./watchtower-notifications.env This output includes the following values:
CONTAINER_ID: the ID of the container that ran notify-upgrade. When notify-upgrade cannot find its own container ID, the line shows instead. Replace it with the container’s name or ID before you run the command, because a shell reads < and > as redirections. FILE_NAME: the name of the temporary file, such as watchtower-notif-urls-1234567890 Run that command to copy the file to your local machine:
docker cp CONTAINER_ID:FILE_NAME ./watchtower-notifications.env The temporary file is automatically removed after 5 minutes or when the container stops, so copy it promptly after generation. If you are running notify-upgrade as a one-off command (docker run --rm ...), the process will wait up to 5 minutes before exiting. Before it writes the file, notify-upgrade checks every URL with Shoutrrr, as Watchtower does at startup. If Shoutrrr rejects a URL, such as a Discord webhook whose ID is not a number, notify-upgrade writes no file. Its error never contains the URL. It usually names the service. It cannot when the URL has no scheme or does not parse. The same holds for a URL that ends in an empty # fragment. The error gives a notification URL’s position, counting from 1. For a URL converted from a legacy notification type, it names that type instead. Shoutrrr’s warnings about a URL, such as a deprecated key, appear in the log. When the conversion fails, notify-upgrade logs the error and exits with code 1. It removes any file it started to write. If it logs “Failed to remove temporary file” instead, delete the file named in that warning yourself, because it can hold your notification credentials.
data.running-the-command#Running the Command: The notify-upgrade can be run either against a Watchtower container that is already running or as a single-run instance that allows you to convert a Docker Compose configuration or Docker CLI flag / environment variable configuration.
data.single-use-run#Single-Use Run:
If you have not yet deployed Watchtower or if you want to run notify-upgrade as a one-off command without starting the persistent Watchtower update loop, then run a temporary container configured with notify-upgrade as the command.
Email (SMTP)GotifySlackMicrosoft Teams Docker ComposeDocker CLI (Env Vars)Docker CLI (Flags) services: watchtower: image: nickfedor/watchtower:latest command: notify-upgrade environment: WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATIONS: email WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER: smtp.example.com WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER_PORT: 587 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER_USER: USERNAME WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER_PASSWORD: 'PASSWORD' WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_FROM: sender@example.com WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_TO: recipient@example.com volumes: - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock docker run --rm \ --name watchtower-notify-upgrade \ -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \ -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATIONS=email \ -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER=smtp.example.com \ -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER_PORT=587 \ -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER_USER=USERNAME \ -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER_PASSWORD='PASSWORD' \ -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_FROM=sender@example.com \ -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_TO=recipient@example.com \ nickfedor/watchtower \ notify-upgrade docker run --rm \ --name watchtower-notify-upgrade \ -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \ nickfedor/watchtower \ notify-upgrade \ --notifications email \ --notification-email-server smtp.example.com \ --notification-email-server-port 587 \ --notification-email-server-user USERNAME \ --notification-email-server-password 'PASSWORD' \ --notification-email-from sender@example.com \ --notification-email-to recipient@example.com Replace the following:
USERNAME: the user name for your SMTP server. notify-upgrade writes an @ in it as %40. PASSWORD: the password for your SMTP server, inside the single quotes. In a Compose file, write each ' in it as '' and each $ as $$. In a shell command, write each ' as '\''. Use your SMTP server’s host name in place of smtp.example.com and your own addresses in place of sender@example.com and recipient@example.com.

Replace the example environment variables with your own legacy notification configuration. The notify-upgrade command inspects the container’s current configuration, so it must be started with your legacy notification settings.

data.overview#Overview:
Watchtower can use Shoutrrr’s Teams service to send Microsoft Teams notifications.
The webhook URL comes from a Power Automate workflow with the “When a Teams webhook request is received” trigger or from an Azure Logic Apps workflow. In Power Automate, set the trigger’s “Who can trigger the flow?” option to “Anyone”. Watchtower sends with the URL’s sig signature and cannot sign in to your tenant. Copy the whole URL from the trigger.
Watchtower checks the webhook URL at startup through Shoutrrr, whether it is set in a teams:// URL or in the legacy option. It must use https:// and carry a sig signature. Its host must be one that Microsoft issues for workflows. Watchtower refuses to start with any other URL, such as a retired Office 365 connector URL on webhook.office.com. Shoutrrr’s webhook URL rules list the accepted hosts.
Power Automate URLs on logic.azure.com Power Automate flows left logic.azure.com on November 30, 2025. Their old URLs on that domain no longer trigger them. Copy the current URL from the flow’s trigger.
Watchtower still accepts logic.azure.com URLs because Azure Logic Apps workflows use that domain.

data.delay#Delay:
Delay before sending notifications expressed in seconds. Watchtower exits at startup if the value is negative.
Argument: --notifications-delay Environment Variable: WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATIONS_DELAY Type: Integer Default: None
data.hostname#Hostname:
Custom hostname specified in subject/title.
Argument: --notifications-hostname Environment Variable: WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATIONS_HOSTNAME Type: String Default: None This is useful for overriding the operating system hostname.
data.level#Level:
Controls the log level for notifications.
Argument: --notifications-level Environment Variable: WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATIONS_LEVEL Type: String Default: info Possible values: panic, fatal, error, warn, info, debug, trace.
data.log-stdout#Log Stdout:
Enable output from logger:// Shoutrrr service to stdout.
Argument: --notification-log-stdout Environment Variable: WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_LOG_STDOUT Type: Boolean Default: false Only the logger:// output goes to stdout. Shoutrrr’s own messages, such as a warning that a service sends without TLS, go to Watchtower’s log at their level.
data.skip-title#Skip Title:
Disable passing the title parameter to notifications.
Argument: --notification-skip-title Environment Variable: WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_SKIP_TITLE Type: Boolean Default: false This will not pass a dynamic title override to notification services. If no title is configured for the service, it will remove the title altogether.
data.split-by-container#Split by Container:
Send a separate notification for each container instead of grouping them.
Argument: --notification-split-by-container Environment Variable: WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_SPLIT_BY_CONTAINER Type: Boolean Default: false By default, notifications are grouped for all updated containers in a single session. When split notifications is enabled, a separate notification is sent for each of these containers: a container that was updated or restarted a container whose update failed a monitor-only container with a newer image a container skipped during its update cooldown Messages that none of these notifications carries are sent after them, one notification per container. A failed update check and a disk-space warning are examples. Messages that name no container are sent together. These notifications carry no report. A report template shows them only if it lists .Entries.
data.title-tag#Title Tag:
Prefix to include in the title.
Argument: --notification-title-tag Environment Variable: WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_TITLE_TAG Type: String Default: None This is useful when running multiple Watchtower instances.

Signal Send notifications via Signal

data.attachments#Attachments:
The Signal service supports sending base64-encoded attachments:
shoutrrr send "signal://localhost:8080/+18005550100/+18005550101" \ "Message with attachment" \ --attachments "ATTACHMENT_1,ATTACHMENT_2" Replace ATTACHMENT_1 and ATTACHMENT_2 with the base64-encoded files to attach.
Attachments must be provided as base64-encoded data. The API server handles MIME type detection and file handling.

data.examples-1#Examples:
Send to a single phone number:
signal://localhost:8080/+18005550100/+18005550101 Send to multiple recipients:

data.overview#Overview:
Watchtower uses Shoutrrr’s Signal service to send Signal notifications.
Signal notifications require a Signal API server that can send messages on behalf of a registered Signal account. This is typically done using signal-cli-rest-api or secured-signal-api .
data.parameters#Parameters: USERNAME: the user name for HTTP Basic Authentication (optional) PASSWORD: the password for HTTP Basic Authentication (optional) HOST: the host name or IP address of the Signal API server PORT: the port of the Signal API server (default: 8080) SOURCE_PHONE: the Signal phone number that sends, with its country code, such as +18005550100 RECIPIENT: a phone number, or a group ID written as group.GROUP_ID, to send to
data.setting-up-a-signal-api-server#Setting u: Phone Number: A dedicated phone number registered with Signal API Server: A server running signal-cli with REST API capabilities Account Linking: Linking the server as a secondary device to your Signal account Optional Security Layer: Authentication and endpoint restrictions via a proxy The server must be able to receive SMS verification codes during initial setup and maintain a persistent connection to Signal’s servers.
data.tls-configuration#TLS Configuration: Use signal:// for HTTPS (default, recommended) Use signal://...?disabletls=yes for HTTP (insecure, for local testing only)

data.enabling-notifications#Enabling Notifica:
To send notifications, use the NOTIFICATION URL configuration option to specify the Shoutrrr service URL.
The Shoutrrr URL follows the format:
SERVICE://[CREDENTIALS[:MORE_CREDENTIALS]@]HOST[/PATH][?KEY=VALUE[&KEY=VALUE...]] This format includes the following values:
SERVICE: the Shoutrrr service, such as discord or telegram CREDENTIALS: the credentials the service needs, such as a token MORE_CREDENTIALS: further credentials, for services that need them HOST: the host or service part of the URL PATH: the path, for services that use one KEY and VALUE: a query parameter and its value Parts in square brackets are optional. Which parts a service uses and what they hold depend on the service. A Gotify URL such as gotify://gotify.example.com/TOKEN has no credentials before its host.
The NOTIFICATION URL configuration option can also reference a file, in which case the contents of the file are used.
Watchtower checks every notification URL when it starts.
Rejected notification URLs
If Shoutrrr cannot use a URL, such as one with no host or with a token that is not in the service’s format, Watchtower logs Failed to initialize notifications and exits.
The error gives the URL’s position, counting from 1. For a URL converted from a legacy notification type, it gives that type instead. The error usually names the service and the problem. It cannot name the service when the URL has no scheme or does not parse. The same holds for a URL that ends in an empty # fragment. The error never contains the URL. When Watchtower runs as its container’s main process, it first sets the container’s restart policy to no, as with any other startup error. The container then does not restart in a loop. If Watchtower cannot find its container or change the policy, it logs an error and still exits with code 1. The container can then restart in a loop.
data.file-based-templates#File-Based Template:
For more complex templates or better maintainability, use the notification-template-file configuration option to specify a path to a template file.
When both inline and file-based templates are specified, the file-based template takes precedence. For detailed information about template syntax, available data structures, and examples, see the Notification Templates documentation.
data.inline-templates#Inline Templates: Use the notification-template configuration option to specify a template directly as a string.
data.notification-templates#Notification Temp: Watchtower allows you to customize the format and content of notification messages using Go templates. You can define templates either inline or load them from a file.
data.overview#Overview: Watchtower uses Shoutrrr to send notifications.
data.startup-notifications#Startup Notificati:
Watchtower will log and send a notification every time it is started.
This behavior can be disabled with the DISABLE STARTUP MESSAGE configuration option.
data.using-multiple-notification-services#Usi:
Watchtower supports using multiple Shoutrrr URLs to send notifications to multiple notification services.
Docker ComposeDocker CLI Docker SecretsSingle-lineMulti-line This is the recommended method for providing Shoutrrr URLs, as they typically contain security-sensitive values.
discord://WEBHOOK_TOKEN@WEBHOOK_ID telegram://BOT_TOKEN@telegram?chats=CHAT_ID secrets: notification_urls: file: ./secrets/notification_urls.txt services: watchtower: image: nickfedor/watchtower:latest volumes: - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock secrets: - notification_urls environment: - WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_URL=/run/secrets/notification_urls restart: unless-stopped Comma or space-separated lists can also be provided to the WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_URL environment variable.
services: watchtower: image: nickfedor/watchtower:latest environment: WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_URL: "discord://WEBHOOK_TOKEN@WEBHOOK_ID,telegram://BOT_TOKEN@telegram?chats=CHAT_ID" volumes: - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock restart: unless-stopped Comma or space-separated lists can also be provided to the WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_URL environment variable.
services: watchtower: image: nickfedor/watchtower:latest environment: WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_URL: > discord://WEBHOOK_TOKEN@WEBHOOK_ID, telegram://BOT_TOKEN@telegram?chats=CHAT_ID volumes: - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock restart: unless-stopped Do NOT define the variable multiple times
Defining WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_URL multiple times in your environment will cause the last value to overwrite previous ones:
# WRONG - Only the second URL will be used: environment: - WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_URL=discord://WEBHOOK_TOKEN@WEBHOOK_ID - WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_URL=telegram://BOT_TOKEN@telegram?chats=CHAT_ID Environment VariableFlags When using the Docker CLI, the --notification-url environment variable can accept a comma or space-separated list.
docker run -d \ --name watchtower \ -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \ -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_URL="discord://WEBHOOK_TOKEN@WEBHOOK_ID,telegram://BOT_TOKEN@telegram?chats=CHAT_ID" \ nickfedor/watchtower When using the Docker CLI, the --notification-url CLI flag can be used multiple times.
docker run -d \ --name watchtower \ -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \ nickfedor/watchtower \ --notification-url "discord://WEBHOOK_TOKEN@WEBHOOK_ID" \ --notification-url "telegram://BOT_TOKEN@telegram?chats=CHAT_ID" Replace the following:
WEBHOOK_TOKEN: the token of your Discord webhook WEBHOOK_ID: the ID of your Discord webhook BOT_TOKEN: the token of your Telegram bot CHAT_ID: the Telegram chat to send to, such as a chat ID or a channel name that starts with @ CLI Flags vs Environment Variables
The CLI flag can be called multiple times as CLI arguments; however, defining the environment variable multiple times will NOT work and only the last value will be used.
This is because CLI flags use a StringArray type that supports multiple invocations, while environment variables are simple key-value pairs that get overwritten when defined multiple times.
For environment variables, use comma-separated or space-separated values.
data.verifying-multiple-notifications#Verifyi:
When Watchtower starts, check the logs for the notification summary:
time="2026-01-28T16:07:24+01:00" level=info msg="Using notifications: discord, telegram" If you only see one service listed (e.g., Using notifications: telegram), your multiple URL configuration was not parsed correctly.

data.changelog-in-the-legacy-notification#Cha:
When the option is enabled and a URL resolves, the default-legacy notification gains one line per updated container:
Changelog: https://github.com/org/app/releases/tag/v1.2.3 Nothing is emitted when the option is off, so a default deployment’s output is unchanged.
data.changelog-resolution#Changelog resolutio:
com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.changelog-url label, with placeholders substituted. A versioned releases URL, when the exact release tag is known. See Versioned release links. An unversioned releases URL built for github.com, gitlab.com, codeberg.org, and for a container that sets com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.git-host. OCI org.opencontainers.image.url. OCI org.opencontainers.image.documentation. An explicit com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.changelog-url label may include placeholders from the new version when known: {major}, {minor}, {patch}, {tag}, {commit}.

An image with only org.opencontainers.image.source still exposes .Source / derived .GitRepo. Git monitoring stays off unless the container is associated and the watcher is on. See Git Monitoring for association and rebuilds.
data.cooldown-report-fields#Cooldown report f:
A container that an image cooldown holds back is listed under .Report.Skipped. Report templates can read the cooldown on it with these fields. They are empty, or the zero time, on a container that no cooldown holds back.
Field Meaning .CooldownDelay The configured cooldown, such as 1 day .CooldownAge Age of the newer image, such as 18 hours. Empty when its age is unavailable. .CooldownRemaining Time until the image is old enough, such as 6 hours. Empty when its age is unavailable. .CooldownEligibleAt Time the image is old enough, as a Go time.Time. The zero time when its age is unavailable. {{- with .Report -}} {{- $sep := "" -}} {{- range .Skipped -}} {{- if .CooldownDelay -}} {{- $sep }}{{ .Name }}: cooldown {{ .CooldownDelay }} {{- with .CooldownRemaining }}, eligible in {{ . }}{{ end -}} {{- $sep = "\n" -}} {{- end -}} {{- end -}} {{- end -}} app: cooldown 1 day, eligible in 6 hours In the template preview, the first skipped container is held back by a cooldown and carries these fields.
data.customizing-templates#Customizing Templa:
You can create custom templates to format notifications differently.
Use the Template Preview Tool to test your templates interactively.
When the preview report toggle is off, simple templates can range over . just as they do in Watchtower. When the report toggle is on, range over .Entries.
