data.examples#Examples:
Create a template file named custom-template.txt with your desired template content, then mount it into the container and specify the path:
Docker ComposeDocker CLI (Env Vars) services: watchtower: image: nickfedor/watchtower:latest environment: WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_TEMPLATE_FILE: "/custom-template.txt" volumes: - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock - TEMPLATE_FILE:/custom-template.txt Replace TEMPLATE_FILE with the path of the template file on the Docker host. A relative path starts with ./ and is read from the Compose project directory, which is the directory of the first Compose file unless you set --project-directory.
docker run -d \ --name watchtower \ -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \ -v "TEMPLATE_FILE:/custom-template.txt" \ -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_TEMPLATE_FILE="/custom-template.txt" \ nickfedor/watchtower:latest Replace TEMPLATE_FILE with the absolute path of the template file on the Docker host.
data.git-and-oci-report-fields#Git and OCI re:
Custom report templates can use these fields on each container. They are populated even when Git monitoring is off.
Field Meaning .GitRepo com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.git-repo, else git-image mapping, else OCI org.opencontainers.image.source .GitRef com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.git-ref (or com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.git-branch), else mapping ref. Empty when the container is not Git-associated. .Changelog com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.changelog-url, else a derived releases URL, else OCI url / documentation .Source OCI org.opencontainers.image.source .ImageURL OCI org.opencontainers.image.url .Documentation OCI org.opencontainers.image.documentation .CurrentImageVersion OCI org.opencontainers.image.version of the running image .LatestImageVersion OCI org.opencontainers.image.version of the newly pulled image. Empty when there is no newer image. .CurrentImageRevision OCI org.opencontainers.image.revision of the running image .LatestImageRevision OCI org.opencontainers.image.revision of the newly pulled image. Empty when there is no newer image. The Current* fields describe the image the container is running, the Latest* fields the image it is moving to. .Changelog, .Source, .ImageURL, and .Documentation are resolved from the latest known image, so they describe the new version once one is found and the running image otherwise.
.GitRef is the configured Git ref and nothing else. An OCI version is never copied into it. Use .CurrentImageVersion or .LatestImageVersion instead.
Because the two versions are separate fields, a template can print the transition:
{{- with .Report -}} {{- range $i, $c := .Updated -}} {{- if $i }} {{ end -}} {{ $c.Name }}: {{ $c.CurrentImageVersion }} → {{ $c.LatestImageVersion }} {{- with $c.Changelog }} {{ . }} {{- end -}} {{- end -}} {{- end -}} app: 1.2.2 → 1.2.3 https://github.com/org/app/releases/tag/v1.2.3 The built-in default report template prints image IDs, the ref, and the changelog on an updated container when they are set:
- app (myapp:latest): abcdef123456 updated to 34567890abcd ref v1.2.4 https://github.com/org/app/releases
data.length-limit#Length limit:
After cleaning, text longer than 1,024 characters keeps its first 511 and last 512 characters with … between them. A long error page or command output then cannot fill a notification. The start of an error usually names the failure, and the end of command output usually holds its result.
The limit applies to each piece of text rather than to the whole message. A notification with many entries can still exceed a service’s own message limit. Watchtower’s own log is not shortened this way.
data.log-lines-from-a-git-update#Log lines fr:
With notification report off, Watchtower sends the log line itself. The default-legacy template formats these messages instead of dumping every field:
Message What the notification says Found new Git revision Found new Git revision: REVISION (SHORT_COMMIT) Built image from Git URL context Built image: IMAGE (IMAGE_ID) Built Compose project Built Compose project: PROJECT (SERVICES), only when containers are not restarted Git build failed. Leaving running container untouched Container and the error. The running container was left in place. Compose apply failed. Docker Compose may have partially recreated services Container and a short failure line. Compose project directory is not readable. Leaving the running container untouched Skipped CONTAINER: compose directory is not readable Skipped container with an invalid git semver policy Skipped CONTAINER: invalid git semver policy Skipped container with an invalid git-host Skipped CONTAINER: invalid git-host These lines include the following values:
REVISION: the repository path and the tag or branch, such as github.com/org/app@v1.2.3 SHORT_COMMIT: the first 12 characters of the commit IMAGE: the built image, such as app:git-0123456789ab IMAGE_ID: the short ID of the built image PROJECT: the Compose project SERVICES: the Compose services that were built, separated by commas CONTAINER: the container name The log fields are container, image, repo, ref, commit, changelog, project, dir, and error. A custom simple template reads them from .Data:
{{- $sep := "" -}} {{- range . -}} {{- if eq .Message "Built image from Git URL context" -}} {{- $sep }}{{ .Data.container }} {{ .Data.commit }} {{ .Data.changelog }} {{- $sep = "\n" -}} {{- end -}} {{- end -}} The json notification report emits the same values under camelCase keys: gitRepo, gitRef, changelog, ociSource, imageUrl, documentation, currentImageVersion, latestImageVersion, currentImageRevision, and latestImageRevision. Porcelain JSON and /v1/check use snake_case instead: git_repo, git_ref, changelog, oci_source, image_url, documentation, current_image_version, latest_image_version, current_revision, and latest_revision.
data.named-templates#Named Templates:
Pass one of these names to notification-template instead of an inline template string:
Name Purpose default Human-readable session summary default-legacy Per-log-entry formatting json.v1 Full notification data as JSON (ToJSON) porcelain.v1.summary-no-log One container per line porcelain.json Stable JSON report (ToPorcelainJSON) porcelain.json is the template selected by --porcelain json. It renders .Report through ToPorcelainJSON and omits log entries. The JSON shape is documented under Programmatic Output (Porcelain).
Available template functions: ToUpper, ToLower, ToJSON, ToPorcelainJSON, Title, RFC1123, HasKey, and FormatDiskSpace.
data.notification-report#Notification Report:
Enables the session report as the notification template data, including container statuses and logs.
Argument: --notification-report Environment Variable: WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_REPORT Type: Boolean Default: false The template is a Go template that processes either a list of log entries (Message, Data, Level, Time) captured from zerolog events or a format.Data struct, depending on the notification-report configuration option.
data.notification-template#Notification Templ:
Sets the Go template used for formatting notification messages.
Argument: --notification-template Environment Variable: WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_TEMPLATE Type: String Default: See default templates below
data.notification-template-file#Notification:
Sets the path to a file containing the Go template used for formatting notification messages.
Argument: --notification-template-file Environment Variable: WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_TEMPLATE_FILE Type: String Default: (empty) When both the notification-template and notification-template-file configuration options are specified, the file-based template takes precedence over the inline template.
data.overview#Overview: You can customize the message posted by setting a notification template.
data.printable-on-one-line#Printable on one l:
Watchtower cleans each piece of text in these ways:
It removes terminal escape sequences, such as colours, window titles and clipboard writes. It removes control characters other than tabs. It removes invisible Unicode format characters, such as bidirectional text controls, zero-width characters and tag characters. Emoji joined with zero-width joiners show as their separate parts. It ends a line at each newline, carriage return and Unicode line or paragraph separator. It joins the trimmed, non-blank lines with |. No value can then start a line that reads like a Watchtower message.
data.report-templates#Report Templates:
When the notification-report configuration option is set, the template processes a format.Data struct containing a session report and log entries.
{{- if .Report -}} {{- with .Report -}} {{len .Scanned}} Scanned, {{len .Updated}} Updated, {{len .Restarted}} Restarted, {{len .Failed}} Failed {{- if ( or .Updated .Restarted .Failed .Skipped ) -}} {{- range .Updated}} - {{.Name}} ({{.ImageName}}): {{.CurrentImageID.ShortID}} updated to {{.LatestImageID.ShortID}}{{with .GitRef}} ref {{.}}{{end}}{{with .Changelog}} {{.}}{{end}} {{- end -}} {{- range .Fresh}} - {{.Name}} ({{.ImageName}}): {{.State}} {{- end -}} {{- range .Restarted}} - {{.Name}} ({{.ImageName}}): {{.State}} {{- end -}} {{- range .Skipped}} - {{.Name}} ({{.ImageName}}): {{.State}}: {{.Error}} {{- end -}} {{- range .Failed}} - {{.Name}} ({{.ImageName}}): {{.State}}: {{.Error}} {{- end -}} {{- end -}} {{- end -}} {{- end -}} {{- if .Entries -}} {{- if .Report }} {{ end -}} Logs: {{- range .Entries }} {{ .Time.Format "2006-01-02T15:04:05Z07:00" }} [{{ .Level }}] {{ .Message }} {{- end -}} {{- end -}} This example generates a summary of container statuses followed by logs, for notifications such as email or Slack messages. Some notifications carry no report. Their .Report is nil. Examples are a check request’s messages and the messages that none of a split session’s container notifications carries. A report template shows them only if it lists .Entries, as this example does. When the notification-split-by-container configuration option is enabled, .Report.Focus is the container the notification is about. It is nil for the report of a whole session, as in the template preview. Read it inside {{ with .Report }}, because .Report.Focus fails the template when .Report is nil. The built-in default report template lists each container by its status instead of the logs. A container with a newer image that Watchtower did not apply is listed as Stale. Examples are a monitor-only container and a skipped Watchtower self-update.

data.text-from-outside-watchtower#Text from o:
Some text in a notification comes from outside Watchtower. That includes lifecycle hook output, image annotations and error messages from registries, the container engine and Git servers. Before a template runs, Watchtower makes that text printable on one line and limits its length. This applies to every log message, log field key and value, and report field, including the values inside nested fields.
The JSON and porcelain templates receive the same values. The title, the host name and the text a template writes itself, including its own line breaks, stay as written. Watchtower does not escape markup or mentions for each notification service, as Lifecycle Hooks describes.

data.versioned-release-links#Versioned releas:
A derived changelog normally points at the release index, for example https://github.com/org/app/releases. A versioned link such as https://github.com/org/app/releases/tag/v1.2.3 is better, but the exact tag spelling cannot be derived from the OCI version alone. A release tag and the version annotation of the same release need not agree on a leading v.
To resolve it, Watchtower confirms which tag actually matches the image it pulled by comparing manifest digests, then uses that tag’s exact spelling.
This costs extra registry requests Resolving the tag issues one or two extra manifest requests per updated container, which roughly doubles that session’s manifest requests for the update.
The lookup is therefore off by default. Enable it per deployment with --enable-changelog or the com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable-changelog label.
A changelog-url label does not enable it. Setting a URL says what the link is, not that a registry request is authorized, so a template referencing {tag} stays unfilled until the option is turned on for that container.
With the option off, the changelog resolves to the unversioned release index and costs no requests. A Git-monitored container never needs the lookup, because its tag comes from the semver policy rather than a registry. Under a policy of none a branch-triggered rebuild resolves no tag, so a template referencing {tag} stays unfilled. A container with no OCI version, a digest-pinned image, and an unknown or unparseable repo host all skip the lookup. A rate limit on the first candidate abandons the probe rather than spend a second request the registry will refuse. Results are cached per session, so sibling containers on the same image only pay once.

data.expected-behavior#Expected Behavior:
When running Watchtower with default settings:
It will monitor all running containers on the host Every 24 hours, it will poll if the monitored containers have updated image digests If an updated image digest is detected, then Watchtower will:
Pull the updated container image Perform a graceful shutdown of the target container and its dependencies Start a new container with the updated image while maintaining the previous container’s configuration
data.overview#Overview: Watchtower is designed to run as a Docker container. It only requires access to the Docker host’s Docker socket in order to interact with the Docker engine. By default, Watchtower will review the monitored containers for image updates. If a container has an updated image, then Watchtower will perform the update task by pulling the new image, stopping the old container, rebuilding the container with the new image, and starting the new container.
